name: Medical Assisting
description: The clinical and administrative support role a physician's office, clinic and urgent-care centre runs on — vital signs, patient history, venipuncture, injections, specimen collection and the medical record, all under a physician's direct supervision. ⚠⚠ Florida defines what a medical assistant may do in statute (s. 458.3485) and requires NO licence, certificate or training to do it. Taught at 38 Florida public institutions, overwhelmingly as a one-to-two-year clock-hour certificate at a district technical college.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ THE PROGRAMME HAS FOUR LABELLED EXIT POINTS, AND ALMOST NOBODY TELLS STUDENTS SO. Florida builds its CTE programmes as OCCUPATIONAL COMPLETION POINTS, and the state prints the OCP letter inside the course title. Medical Assisting runs: OCP A Basic Healthcare Worker (HSC0003, 90 hours) — OCP B Phlebotomist (MEA0520, 75 hours) — OCP C Phlebotomist, MA (MEA0521, 75 hours) — OCP D EKG Aide, MA (MEA0543, 75 hours) — OCP E Medical Assistant, three courses of 320 hours each. ⚠⚠ Each of the first four is a JOB TITLE you can leave on and be hired for. A student who completes OCP B can work as a phlebotomist, earn, and come back for the rest; a student who stops at OCP D is an EKG aide. ⚠ The whole thing is roughly 1,300 clock hours, and you do not have to do it in one run. Ask any programme where its OCPs fall and whether it will award the intermediate certificates — not every institution issues them even though the state structures the programme around them. ⚠⚠ Note the credential level: of 485 Florida credentials awarded in 2023, 441 were one-to-two-year certificates and only 26 were associate degrees. This is a CLOCK-HOUR programme, not a degree, and clock hours do not transfer into a degree the way credits do. If a nursing or health-science degree is the eventual goal, say so at the start and ask what articulates.

cips.note: Medical/Clinical Assistant — 38 Florida public institutions and 485 credentials in 2023, 441 of them one-to-two-year certificates. The great majority of carriers are DISTRICT TECHNICAL COLLEGES, which is where Florida actually teaches this.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The closest comparison, and the contrast is worth understanding before choosing. Almost identical pay ($45,690 against $45,750), almost identical training length, similar institutions — but Florida REQUIRES a pharmacy technician to register with the Board of Pharmacy and complete a board-approved programme, and requires nothing at all of a medical assistant. ⚠ And the ladders run the other way: medical assisting has four labelled exit points, pharmacy technology has none.

⚠ The usual next step, and the honest warning is about credit. Medical assisting is a CLOCK-HOUR programme and nursing is a credit programme, so the hours do not simply carry over — what transfers is the clinical confidence, the terminology and, at many institutions, an articulated block for the Basic Healthcare Worker core. Ask the nursing programme in writing what it will accept BEFORE you enrol in medical assisting expecting it to count.

⚠ Where the phlebotomy exit point can lead. OCP B and OCP C of medical assisting are phlebotomist certificates, and phlebotomy is the entry rung of the clinical laboratory. A medical assistant who found the specimen-collection half the interesting part has a short, well-defined route into laboratory work — and the laboratory ladder goes considerably further, to MLT and then MLS.

The same shape in a different setting: a short technical-college certificate assisting a licensed practitioner, taught largely at the same institutions. ⚠ Named because students comparing short allied-health certificates are usually comparing these two, and the dental one is smaller and more specialised.
